prompt: How many 20th-century paintings have been sold for at least $100 million (in nominal sale price) at Christie’s New York since 2020?
answer:
**Six** 20th-century paintings have sold for at least **$100 million nominally** at Christie’s New York since 2020:

| Year | Painting | Sale price |
|---|---|---:|
| 2021 | Pablo Picasso, *Femme assise près d’une fenêtre (Marie-Thérèse)* | $103.4m |
| 2022 | Andy Warhol, *Shot Sage Blue Marilyn* | $195.04m |
| 2022 | Gustav Klimt, *Birch Forest* | $104.585m |
| 2023 | Pablo Picasso, *Femme à la montre* | about $139.4m |
| 2024 | René Magritte, *L’empire des lumières* | about $121.2m |
| 2025 | Jackson Pollock, *Number 7A, 1948* | $181.185m |

The other Paul G. Allen Collection works listed above $100 million—by Seurat, Cézanne, van Gogh and Gauguin—were 19th-century paintings, while Brancusi’s *Danaïde* was a sculpture, so they are excluded.
